key_insight: BRDFusion combines physics-based inverse rendering with generative video modeling to get the best of both worlds: controllable lighting and geometry from physical modeling, plus realism from generation. It aims to reconstruct urban scenes more faithfully while reducing common artifacts.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of inverse rendering urban scenes from video, where physics-based methods can be accurate but artifact-prone, and generative methods can look realistic but often lack consistency and control.
method: Unifies inverse rendering and forward rendering in a single framework.
Combines a physically-based model for controllability with a generative model for realism.
Targets urban-scene reconstruction from captured videos to improve both visual quality and physical consistency.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical direction for building rendering systems that are both photorealistic and physically grounded. It could improve workflows in content creation, digital twins, and autonomous driving simulation.

paper_title: BRDFusion: Physics Meets Generation for Urban Scene Inverse Rendering
paper_authors: Yi-Ruei Liu, Jie-Ying Lee, Zheng-Hui Huang, Yu-Lun Liu, Chih-Hao Lin
